messages.subject: specify test set and reference set
parts:
Hi Henrik,

>     3) "For each location, the raw CN is calculated as the chip effect relative
> to the chip effect of a normal reference sample.  If no reference sample is
> available, a robust average across all samples can be used instead."

        Sorry that I did not state my 3rd question clearly.

        My question is how to specify the test set (e.g. ScottH_2007 in your example) and the normal reference set, which
may include the test set, (e.g. AGRF_2007a) in the script.

        In your document of "Total copy number analysis 500k":
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis

       Only the normal reference set is specified,  test set is not specified:

... ...
Test set: ScottH_2007

Test samples: 1-288, 2-437, 3-575, 414-VA (250K Nsp & 250K Sty; part of the below reference set)



Reference set: AGRF_2007a

Reference samples: 51 Nsp and 27 Sty chips (including above 4 samples).

Location: rawData/AGRF_2007a/Mapping250K_Nsp/ and rawData/AGRF_2007a/Mapping250K_Sty/

... ...
name <- "AGRF_2007a"

... ...

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName(name, chipType=chipType)


       I did not see how ScottH_2007 is used. In my case, I have 7 ovarian cancer samples (snp arrays) that I want to use as the test set, and I want
to use all different cancer samples including these 7 ovarian cancer samples as the normal reference set. The desired outcome would be that the raw CN is calculated as the chip effect from 7 ovarian samples relative  to the chip effect of all of cancer reference samples.  How do I specify these two sets ?

        Thanks,

Qicheng
---------------------------------------------------------------
Hi.
On Fri, Dec 5, 2008 at 7:50 AM, Qicheng Ma <qicheng...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Henrik,

>        Thanks for your reply,  I have 3 more questions after reading your
> email:

> 1) I read through your instruction of total copy number analysis for 500k,
> there is no instruction on how to generate  cesN object in "theta <-
> extractTheta(cesN, units=units, drop=TRUE)" you mentioned in
> http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/...

That is the ChipEffectSet you typically get out from doing
fragment-length normalization, cf.

  http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number...

In that vignette 'cesN' corresponds to cesNList[[chipType]].  Since
you have two chip types you will get two different 'cesN' objects.  If
you use extractTheta() on these, you'll have to merge the theta
yourself.  So, you have to be careful.   It is much easier if you just
work of a single chip type.

> 2) I have 7 samples for the ovarian cancer dataset (7 Nsp and and 7 Sty),
> when  I used  extractRawCopyNumbers to extract Copy Numbers for each sample,
> why do  I need to loop over 14 arrays instead of 7 arrays to get all the
> information, since Nsp and Sty are combined into a virtual chip ?

There are 14 hybridizations but only 7 samples.  You only need to
"loop over" the 7 samples (argument still called 'arrays' for various
reasons).  You *must* make sure that you get the names correct for Nsp
and Sty so that the package can pair them up for you.  If you don't,
it will think that there are 14 samples where 7 where hyb'ed on Nsp
and the other 7 on Sty.

When you do

  cbs <- CbsModel(cesNList);
  print(cbs);

make sure that it reports 7 arrays and you can check the names by

  print(getNames(cbs));

> 3) "For each location, the raw CN is calculated as the chip effect relative
> to the chip effect of a normal reference sample.  If no reference sample is
> available, a robust average across all samples can be used instead.", If I
> would like to use SNP arrays for all the tumor types as the reference
> sample, how can I specify this reference sample when I calculate CN for
> these 7 ovarian cancer samples.

I'm not use what you mean by "to use SNP arrays" - do you have another
set of samples you haven't mentioned above?

If you don't specify any reference, the robust average of all samples
will be used.  So, if you have 7 cancer samples from the beginning and
don't specify the reference, the pool of them will be used as the
reference.

Hope this helps

Henrik

I think I understand now. You have a set of samples, say samples
i=1,2,...,I. You want to use all to for the reference (as the robust
average of all). The samples of interest are a subset of these I
samples. Correct?

Then you don't have to do anything particular. Just specify put all
samples together when you preprocess/summarize the data. Then pass
all arrays to the segmentation method you will use and pass this to
the ChromosomeExplorer. Then tell the CE which arrays you are
interested in using setArrays().

This is illustrated in the Vignette 'Total copy number analysis (10K,
100K, 500K)', which you are referring to. Note that the samples of
interest (set "ScottH_2007") are part of the bigger data set
("AGRF_2007a") as indicated in Section 'Setup'. So, when we set up
the 'cs' object, it contains all samples. Then we process the data
until we get fragment-length normalized data sets from both chip types
(cesNList). We pass cesNList to the GladModel (or CbsModel if you
wish), which we then pass to ChromosomeExplorer, e.g.

glad <- GladModel(cesNList)
ce <- ChromosomeExplorer(glad)

This far all samples are processed and carried through. Then we do:

setArrays(ce, c("1-288", "2-437", "3-575", "414-VA"))
setAlias(ce, "ScottH_etal_2007")

which will tell CE (and GLAD) that we are only interested in four
specific samples, and that we wish to call the output/result set
"ScottH_etal_2007" (instead of the default "AGRF_2007a").

FYI, internally in the segmentation method (GladModel), the robust
average is calculated across all samples. This is why you need to
process and keep all arrays up until this point.

Hope this clarifies things

Henrik
